newsitem.title: USA: Sun climbs after Q2 EPS tops consensus.
newsitem.headline: Sun climbs after Q2 EPS tops consensus.

text.p: Shares of Sun Microsystems Inc firmed in after-hours trading after the company reported second-quarter earnings that topped Wall Street estimates.
Shares of Sun traded as high as 29-1/4 in after-hours dealings after the company reported earnings per share of $0.46 for its second fiscal quarter ended December 29, 1996.

Wall Street's consensus estimate was for earnings per share of $0.42, according to a First Call survey. The stock had closed down 5/8 at 28-1/4 on the Nasdaq market. The earnings release was issued after the market close.
Analysts' earnings estimates ranged from $0.39 a share to $0.46 for the quarter, according to First Call.
Sun said revenues for the second quarter were a record $2.08 billion, up nearly 19 percent from the year-ago period.

"The current fiscal year continues to yield strong financial results," Sun Microsystems Chief Financial Officer Michael Lehman said in a statement. "Sun is winning big in corporate intranets, the Internet, and the extranet."
Lehman said the company's investments in research and development and sales and support infrastructure were paying off as it moved to broaden its global presence.
